Under this circumstance, a person who elects to submit reports to the applicant of the final product shall maintain a record of this action [1].

- 21 CFR 211.25 [4]: Each person engaged in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall have education, training, and experience, or any combination thereof, to enable that person to perform the assigned functions. Training shall be in the particular operations that the employee performs and in current good manufacturing practice (including the current good manufacturing practice regulations in this chapter and written procedures required by these regulations) as they relate to the employee's functions. Training in current good manufacturing practice shall be conducted by qualified individuals on a continuing basis and with sufficient frequency to assure that employees remain familiar with CGMP requirements applicable to them.

- 21 CFR 211.28 [5]: Personnel engaged in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall wear clean clothing appropriate for the duties they perform. - 21 CFR 211.34 [6]: Consultants advising on the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of drug products shall have sufficient education, training, and experience, or any combination thereof, to advise on the subject for which they are retained. Records shall be maintained stating the name, address, and qualifications of any consultants and the type of service they provide.

- 21 CFR 211.42 [7]: Design and construction features. Any building or buildings used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall be of suitable size, construction and location to facilitate cleaning, maintenance, and proper operations.

- 21 CFR 211.44 [8]: Lighting. Adequate lighting shall be provided in all areas.

- 21 CFR 211.46 [9]: Ventilation, air filtration, air heating and cooling. Adequate ventilation shall be provided.

- 21 CFR 211.48 [10]: Plumbing. Potable water shall be supplied under continuous positive pressure in a plumbing system free of defects that could contribute contamination to any drug product. Potable water shall meet the standards prescribed in the Environmental Protection Agency's Primary Drinking Water Regulations set forth in 40 CFR part 141. Water not meeting such standards shall not be permitted in the potable water system.

- 21 CFR 211.50 [11]: Sewage, trash, and other refuse in and from the building and immediate premises shall be disposed of in a safe and sanitary manner.

- 21 CFR 211.52 [12]: Adequate washing facilities shall be provided, including hot and cold water, soap or detergent, air driers or single-service towels, and clean toilet facilities easily accessible to working areas.

- 21 CFR 211.56 [13]: Sanitation. Any building used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition, and any such building shall be free of infestation by rodents, birds, insects, and other vermin (other than laboratory animals).

- 21 CFR 211.58 [14]: Maintenance. Any building used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall be maintained in a good state of repair.

- 21 CFR 211.63 [15]: Equipment design, size, and location. Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall be of appropriate design, adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use and for its cleaning and maintenance.

- 21 CFR 211.65 [16]: Equipment construction. Equipment shall be constructed so that surfaces that contact components, in-process materials, or drug products shall not be reactive, additive, or absorptive so as to alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements.

- 21 CFR 211.67 [17]: Equipment cleaning and maintenance. Equipment and utensils shall be cleaned, maintained, and, as appropriate for the nature of the drug, sanitized and/or sterilized at appropriate intervals to prevent malfunctions or contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements.

- 21 CFR 211.68 [18]: Automatic, mechanical, and electronic equipment. Automatic, mechanical, or electronic equipment or related systems that will perform a function satisfactorily, may be used in the manufacture, processing, packing, and holding of a drug product. If such equipment is so used, it shall be routinely calibrated, inspected, or checked according to a written program designed to assure proper performance. Written records of those calibration checks and inspections shall be maintained.

It states that retailers are not required to submit serious adverse event reports for dietary supplements unless they have a distributor's name on the label and they have an agreement with the manufacturer or packer. If a retailer's name appears on the label, they may authorize the manufacturer or packer to submit reports to the FDA. Additionally, the guidance specifies that dietary supplements must be labeled as such and intended for ingestion, and they cannot be represented as a food or a sole item of a meal or diet. The guidance also notes that the Dietary Supplement and Nonprescription Drug Consumer Protection Act does not apply to foods other than dietary supplements, and there are no other mandatory reporting requirements for such foods. The quality control unit shall be responsible for approving or rejecting drug products manufactured, processed, packed, or held under contract by another company.  
[4] 21 CFR 211.25(a) [4]: Each person engaged in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall have education, training, and experience, or any combination thereof, to enable that person to perform the assigned functions. Training shall be in the particular operations that the employee performs and in current good manufacturing practice (including the current good manufacturing practice regulations in this chapter and written procedures required by these regulations) as they relate to the employee's functions. Training in current good manufacturing practice shall be conducted by qualified individuals on a continuing basis and with sufficient frequency to assure that employees remain familiar with CGMP requirements applicable to them.  
[5] 21 CFR 211.28(a) [5]: Personnel engaged in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall wear clean clothing appropriate for the duties they perform. Protective apparel, such as head, face, hand, and arm coverings, shall be worn as necessary to protect drug products from contamination.  
[6] 21 CFR 211.34 [6]: Consultants advising on the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of drug products shall have sufficient education, training, and experience, or any combination thereof, to advise on the subject for which they are retained. [8] 21 CFR 211.44 [8]: Adequate lighting shall be provided in all areas.  
[9] 21 CFR 211.46(a) [9]: Adequate ventilation shall be provided.  
[10] 21 CFR 211.48(a) [10]: Potable water shall be supplied under continuous positive pressure in a plumbing system free of defects that could contribute contamination to any drug product. Water not meeting such standards shall not be permitted in the potable water system.  
[11] 21 CFR 211.50 [11]: Sewage, trash, and other refuse in and from the building and immediate premises shall be disposed of in a safe and sanitary manner.  
[12] 21 CFR 211.52 [12]: Adequate washing facilities shall be provided, including hot and cold water, soap or detergent, air driers or single-service towels, and clean toilet facilities easily accessible to working areas.  
[13] 21 CFR 211.56(a) [13]: Any building used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall be maintained in a clean and sanitary condition, Any such building shall be free of infestation by rodents, birds, insects, and other vermin (other than laboratory animals). Trash and organic waste matter shall be held and disposed of in a timely and sanitary manner.  
[14] 21 CFR 211.58 [14]: Any building used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall be maintained in a good state of repair.  
[15] 21 CFR 211.63 [15]: Equipment used in the manufacture, processing, packing, or holding of a drug product shall be of appropriate design, adequate size, and suitably located to facilitate operations for its intended use and for its cleaning and maintenance.  
[16] 21 CFR 211.65(a) [16]: Equipment shall be constructed so that surfaces that contact components, in-process materials, or drug products shall not be reactive, additive, or absorptive so as to alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements.  
[17] 21 CFR 211.67(a) [17]: Equipment and utensils shall be cleaned, maintained, and, as appropriate for the nature of the drug, sanitized and/or sterilized at appropriate intervals to prevent malfunctions or contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality, or purity of the drug product beyond the official or other established requirements.  
[18] 21 CFR 211.68(a) [18]: Automatic, mechanical, or electronic equipment or other types of equipment, including computers, or related systems that will perform a function satisfactorily, may be used in the manufacture, processing, packing, and holding of a drug product. If such equipment is so used, it shall be routinely calibrated, inspected, or checked according to a written program designed to assure proper performance. Written records of those calibration checks and inspections shall be maintained.  
[19] 21 CFR 211.80(a) [19]: There shall be written procedures describing in sufficient detail the receipt, identification, storage, handling, sampling, testing, and approval or rejection of components and drug product containers and closures; such written procedures shall be followed.
